looks_like_me_why: Mostly hits — hijab kept, skin tone, thick brows, large brown eyes and overall face shape match the selfie (pages I notice this most: cover, pages 1–4, 8–10, 18). What's off — stylized proportions (bigger eyes, softer jaw) and exaggerated expressions make it clearly a caricature rather than a photo-real likeness. A few indoor frames (pages 11–14) show slightly different cheek/forehead proportions and harder lighting that make the face feel less 'me'.
rings_true_why: Follows the classic Little Red Riding Hood beats and reads like a children's picture book — clear scene progression, short lines per spread, friendly illustration style. Tone and pacing work for young readers. Minor nit: a couple of microcopy choices (ALL CAPS on page 13) feel louder than the rest of the text, but the narrative arc is faithful and coherent.
professional_why: High production values — consistent art direction, polished lighting, cohesive color palette, and strong character design. Composition and props are thoughtful (basket, cottage details). Things that stop it from being a full 'published book' level: occasional awkward cropping/composition choices, a couple of frames where expression + text feel misaligned, and jarring microcopy (all-caps shouting). Overall very close to publishable.
not_good:
- Page 5–7: tight close-ups/cropping on hands and flowers feel a bit claustrophobic; consider more breathing space.
- Pages 11–14 (Grandma's bed): wolf close-ups are very aggressive; for a preschool audience the teeth/angry poses read harsher than earlier frames — tonal mismatch.
- Page 13: ALL CAPS "BIG TEETH" is jarring microcopy; use emphasis instead of full caps.
- Page 15: text says "woodcutter burst through the door" but the illustration (page 15) feels staged/calm — mismatch between action copy and visual affordance.
- Page 16–17 continuity: the wolf jumping out then wardrobe reveal of Grandma is fine narratively but visually it reads like a sudden jump cut; add a bridging frame or visual cue to smooth it.
- Some facial proportion inconsistencies between outdoor and indoor lighting (not every frame feels like the exact same character model).
liked:
- Preserving the hijab and my general features — important and well handled.
- Color and lighting: warm, storybook palette; consistent mood across spreads.
- Composition: strong silhouettes and readable poses; character silhouettes read well even at thumbnail size.
- Props and set dressing: cottage, basket, quilt, and woodcutter tools add narrative affordances that help tell the story without extra text.
- Overall polish: feels like a boutique personalized book I'd be proud to gift after a couple of small fixes.
